chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, all of them from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something from the obligatory inheritance shares, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I bring out for you the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?' So I said, 'The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not been studied.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not been studied?' So he (peace be upon him) brought it out, and it was a splendid book, and therein was: a man who died and left his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle. He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the paternal uncle is two-thirds and for the maternal uncle is the one-third'.

key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of paternal and maternal uncles according to the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the authority of the 'Book of Ali' (Kitab Ali), a specialized legal text attributed to Imam Ali (AS) that was preserved within the scholarly circles but not widely disseminated, underscoring the depth of the Ahl al-Bayt's independent juridical reasoning. It establishes a specific inheritance distribution where the paternal uncle receives two-thirds and the maternal uncle one-third, a ruling that reflects the Shia emphasis on the nuanced application of Quranic principles through the Imams' teachings. This narration serves as a key evidence for the validity of the Imams' legal compilations alongside the Quran in Shia jurisprudence.
